introduction:
A Death Certificate in Maharashtra is a vital legal document that serves as the official proof of an individual's demise. Registering the death is essential for resolving inheritance, insurance claims, property transfer, and bank accounts.

Here is a complete, simple, and step-by-step guide to registering a death and applying for a death certificate in Maharashtra.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Time Limit: A death must ideally be registered within 21 days of its occurrence. Registration within this period is free.
  • Issuing Authority: Gram Panchayat (for rural/villages) and Municipal Corporation / Municipal Council (for urban/cities).
  • Cost: Free (if registered within 21 days). A nominal fee of ₹10 to ₹50 applies for the physical copy or late registration.
  • Processing Time: Usually 5 to 15 days (delayed registrations beyond a month can take 30 to 60 days).
  • Hospital vs. Home Death: If the death occurs in a hospital, the hospital staff directly reports and registers it. If it occurs at home, the Head of Family is responsible for registering it.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: Keep clean photocopies and scanned copies (for online application) of the following ready:
Proof of Death
  • Medical Certificate of Cause of Death: Provided by the hospital or the doctor who attended the deceased.
  • For Delayed Registration: If registering after 1 year, a special order from an Executive Magistrate is required.
Identity Proofs
  • Deceased ID: Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, Ration Card, or PAN Card.
  • Applicant ID: Aadhaar Card or Voter ID of the family member applying.
Address Proof
  • Deceased Address Proof (Any one): Ration card, electricity bill, or Aadhaar showing the deceased's residential address.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Apply Online via Aaple Sarkar Portal

Maharashtra allows you to apply for and download death certificates through the official online portal:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Visit Portal: Go to the official website aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in.
  2. Register: Click on "New User? Register Here" and create an account using your mobile number, Aadhaar, and OTP.
  3. Select Department: Log in, and on the dashboard, search for your local department:
    • Select Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department if the death happened in a village.
    • Select your Municipal Corporation/Urban Local Body if it happened in a city.
  4. Select Service: Select the service named Death Certificate (मृत्यु नोंद दाखला).
  5. Fill Form: Fill in the online form with exact details (Name, Date of Death, Place of Death, etc.).
  6. Upload & Submit: Upload PDFs/scanned copies of the required documents, submit, and pay the small portal fee online.
Offline Visits & Hospital Registrations:
  • No SRO Visit: If registered on time, zero offline visits are needed. The digitally signed certificate will be delivered to your online account. For discrepancies or highly delayed cases, physical document verification at the local Ward Office or Gram Panchayat may be required.
  • Direct Download: If a hospital has already reported and registered the death, you do not need to apply. Simply visit crsorgi.gov.in, search for the deceased's name and date of death, and download the certificate directly.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Register Offline at local administrative office

If you find the online portal confusing, you can register in person:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Identify Local Office: Go to the Gram Panchayat Office (meet the Gram Sevak) if you live in a village, or the Municipal Ward Office / Health Department if in a city.
  2. Collect Form: Ask the counter clerk for a "Death Registration Form".
  3. Fill Out Details: Fill out the details carefully. Ensure the English and Marathi spellings exactly match the deceased person's Aadhaar card.
  4. Attach Documents: Attach photocopies of all required documents (Doctor's MCCD certificate, Aadhaar copies).
  5. Submission: Submit the physical file to the officer and receive your acknowledgment receipt/slip.
  6. Collection: Visit the office again after 5 to 7 days (or on the receipt date) to collect the official printed Death Certificate.
afterApplying:
After Applying — What Next?

Track Status & Download

Track status on the Aaple Sarkar portal using your Application Number. Once approved, the certificate is issued with a digitally signed QR code that is legally valid everywhere without a physical stamp or signature.

Printing & Validity

You can print color copies of the downloaded digital certificate at any local service provider. These copies hold complete official validity.

Critical Usage

Keep multiple copies safe. You will need them immediately to claim life insurance, transfer property/vehicles to nominees, close bank accounts, and apply for a Legal Heir or Succession certificate.
